title: Point Density Measures: A Measure-Theoretic Framework with Applications to Geometric Probability
summary: The notion of point density is widely used in geometry, probability, sampling theory, computational science, and spatial statistics to describe the distribution of discrete point sets. Although commonly interpreted as the number of points per unit volume, the concept is often used without a unified measure-theoretic formulation, leading to ambiguities between counting measures, empirical measures, sampling measures, intensity measures, and density functions.
